q: The fundamental test distinguishing capital from revenue expenditure is whether the expenditure ___.

options.A: Creates or adds to a capital asset

q: Which of the following is revenue expenditure?

options.A: Construction of a new railway line

q: Revenue expenditure of Railways is met from ___.
Ordinary Working Expenses of Railways are charged to ___.
Which of the following is NOT part of Ordinary Working Expenses?

options.A: Repairs and maintenance of permanent way

q: Expenditure on fuel (coal, diesel, traction power) for locomotives is charged to ___.
Salaries of station staff are charged to ___.
Day-to-day track maintenance like packing and patrolling is ___.

options.B: Charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Revenue expenditure under repairs and maintenance

q: Renewal of rails with rails of the same section is normally financed from ___.
When old rails are replaced by heavier rails, the extra cost of betterment is charged to ___.
Depreciation on railway assets is charged to revenue by way of ___.

options.C: Annual appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund

q: The Depreciation Reserve Fund provides for ___.
Depreciation is NOT provided on ___.
Pension payments to retired railway servants are debited to ___.
The Pension Fund is fed by ___.
Interest paid on Provident Fund balances of railway staff is charged to ___.
Expenditure on railway hospitals and staff amenities is ___.

options.B: Revenue expenditure under staff welfare and amenities
options.C: Charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund

q: Maintenance of signalling and telecommunication equipment is charged to ___.

options.C: Repairs and Maintenance — Plant and Equipment

q: Running allowances paid to loco pilots and guards are ___.

options.B: Charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund

q: Expenditure which is neither Capital nor Ordinary Working Expenses is classified as ___.
New minor works on open lines, below the prescribed monetary limit, are charged to ___.
A suspense head in railway accounts is used for ___.

options.C: Expenditure awaiting final classification or adjustment

q: Advances of travelling allowance to staff, pending adjustment, are first debited to ___.
The value of stores purchased but not yet issued for consumption is held under ___.
Expenditure in railway workshops on manufacture of stores is first booked to ___.
Charged expenditure differs from voted expenditure in that it ___.

options.C: Is not submitted to the vote of Parliament

q: Which of the following is 'charged' on the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.D: Salaries and allowances of the President of India

q: Railway Demands for Grants are now presented to Parliament as part of ___.
A Demand for Grant lapses ___.

options.B: At the end of the financial year

q: Expenditure in excess of the grant voted by Parliament requires ___.
Transfer of provision from one sub-head to another within the same grant is called ___.
The operating ratio of Indian Railways expresses ___ as a percentage of gross traffic receipts.

options.A: Ordinary Working Expenses (including appropriations to DRF and Pension Fund)

q: Railway 'net revenue' is arrived at by deducting ___ from gross traffic receipts.
Compensation claims paid for goods lost in transit are charged to ___.
Expenditure on restoration of traffic after an accident is ___.

options.C: Charged to revenue as working expenses
options.D: Met from the staff benefit fund

q: The cost of printing tickets and stationery at stations is ___.

options.B: Charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund

q: Repairs to staff quarters are charged to ___.
Expenditure on the Railway Protection Force is ___.

options.C: Charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund

q: Running of railway training institutes is charged to ___.
Lubricants consumed by rolling stock are charged to ___.
Wages of casual labour engaged for track maintenance are ___.

options.C: Debited to the Depreciation Reserve Fund

q: Before the Railway Budget merger, Railways paid ___ to General Revenues on capital-at-charge.
Interest on loans taken by Railways is charged to ___.
The Depreciation Reserve Fund, which finances renewals, is itself created by ___.
A supplementary grant is sought when ___.

options.A: The sanctioned provision proves insufficient during the year

q: Money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India only under authority of ___.

options.B: An Appropriation Act passed by Parliament

q: Which account records the day-to-day working of Railways — earnings and working expenses?
The cost of uniforms supplied to railway staff is ___.

options.B: Charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund

q: Expenditure on overhauling of wagons in workshops is charged to ___.

options.A: Revenue — Repairs and Maintenance of Carriages and Wagons

q: Savings under a grant which are no longer required should be ___.
